Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football | National World Cup Visa Scandal: Yaw Ampofo Ankrah ‘200% confident’ of exoneration Source : Haruna Mubarak 19 October 2026 10:56am Yaw Ampofo Ankrah Audio By Carbonatix
Suspended National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has expressed “200%” confidence that he will be exonerated by the Presidency over his alleged involvement in the World Cup visa scandal.
Ankrah was suspended by President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday, October 1, following allegations over visa facilitation arrangement linked to the global showpiece.
The controversy followed allegations that about US$623,000 had been received from prospective travellers seeking assistance with visa applications and travel arrangements for the tournament.
About 90 people reportedly paid between $10,000 and $15,000 each, but only five of them obtained visas.
“I’m 200% confident that I’ll be exonerated,” he said during Ghana's Beach Soccer AFCON qualifier against Nigeria.
“People should be very cautious about what they put out there that they cannot verify,” he said, calling on journalists to verify their sources and report the developments professionally.
“I’m very happy that so far the investigations have gone very smoothly, and we’re just waiting for the final report to be released,” he added.
Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong has since been appointed acting Director-General of the National Sports Authority following Ankrah’s suspension.
